# Rear hatch lift angle modification

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Support the rear gate with a rope or strap to relieve weight from the struts. [t1691]

[Partial] Flip the rear strut assembly upside down after removing it from its mounting ball. [t1691]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Support the rear gate with a rope or strap to relieve weight from the struts.
2. Remove the strut mounting brackets using a 10mm wrench.

_Procedure reported by [t1691]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/how-to-make-your-rear-hatch-raise-higher-for-free.2627/>_

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1691] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Remove the rear strut from its mounting ball.
2. [Partial] Flip the entire strut assembly upside down.

</details>

## Tools

- Flat head screwdriver [t1691]

## Parts

- Rear hatch struts: Factory or aftermarket [t1691]

## Specifications

- **Bracket bolt size**: 10mm [t1691] ([Unverified] single report)

## Tips & gotchas

- Switching struts changes the mount offset from in to out, allowing a higher swing arc. [t1691]
- [Partial] Bolt the stud on first when mounting for easier alignment. [t1691]
- [Partial] Use a flathead to pop off the metal collar on the ball joint for easier removal. [t1691]
- Pulling tabs is often easier than unbolting completely. [t1691]
